content.title: Tactile Climb | Contact Risk Releases into Summit Scale
content.summary: Introduce one adult as a small figure against an overwhelming vertical goal, then prove tool bites, unstable holds, and bodily recovery in close views. Preserve equipment and direction after every setback, and release the accumulated effort through a stable summit wide shot.

quick_start.input_format: adult climber as a small subject before a giant vertical goal + at least three load-bearing contacts proved close + one failed contact, visible loss, and explicit braking recovery in the same geography + three equipment identity anchors persist across scales + crossing the final edge releases into a stable summit wide without celebration
quick_start.recommended_input: An adult technician climbs a vertical wind-turbine blade toward its nacelle above the clouds. One hand pad releases; an orange rope visibly arrests the fall before the technician regains footing, crosses the rim, and appears small beside the full hub in a steady wide shot.
required_anchors: Establish one adult climber as a small figure against one dominant vertical objective.
Show at least three distinct load-bearing contacts in tactile close evidence.
Preserve at least three equipment or costume anchors across every scale change.
Cross the ridge close, then end on one stable wide proving arrival without celebration.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Introduce one adult as a small figure against an overwhelming vertical goal, then prove tool bites, unstable holds, and bodily recovery in close views. Preserve equipment and direction after every setback, and release the accumulated effort through a stable summit wide shot.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Establish one original clearly adult climber as a small readable figure against a single overwhelming vertical objective. Alternate environmental scale views with tactile close evidence of at least three different load-bearing contacts such as tool bite, foot placement and rope tension. Introduce one recoverable contact failure that visibly lowers or rotates the adult, then show the arrest and a new valid placement in the same geography before ascent continues. Preserve at least three equipment and costume anchors throughout. Cross the final ridge in close view, then release into one stable wide that proves summit arrival and completed scale without celebration. The reusable mechanism is scale objective, tactile contact evidence, one recoverable failure, continuity-bearing equipment, ridge crossing and summit-scale release—not the source woman, face, clothing, ice axes, mountain, K2 claim, exact stunt, camera, creator identity or timing.
